title: performance(canary): dynamic-threshold autodetection + rollout guards
author: Aditi Rao
description: Motivation: improve automatic detection of latency/throughput regressions observed by the perf-canary pipeline and add conservative rollout guards to prevent noisy canary signal from causing false-positive rollbacks. Summary: implement a dynamic threshold detector that computes per-population latency baselines using exponentially-weighted quantiles, add hysteresis and minimum sample requirements, expose new configuration for per-model and per-route sensitivity, integrate detectors with the rollout controller to gate traffic increases, and add end-to-end perf canary tests and dashboards. This change includes: 1) runtime/detector: new detector 'dynamic_threshold_v2' with EWMA-quantile baseline and hysteresis windows; 2) canary-agent: sample aggregation improvements and minimum-sample enforcement; 3) rollout-controller: pre-rollout gating based on detector verdicts, automatic cooldown periods and safe-fallback policy; 4) telemetry: new metrics (canary.detected_regressions, canary.hysteresis_state, canary.sample_count) and tracing spans for detection decisions; 5) config: canary policy schema extended (sensitivity, min_samples, hysteresis_window); 6) tests/docs: unit tests for detector, integration perf tests in perf-canary lab, migration notes in docs. Testing: local unit tests, CI integration tests against perf-canary harness, manual canary run in staging with synthetic load. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout (ff:perf/dynamic-threshold), enable on staging for 48h, then canary rollout to 5% traffic with automatic rollback if detector flags confirmed regression for >2 consecutive windows. Related: ENG-4921 (detector logic) and SUP-8842 (support case about noisy rollouts).

Aditi Rao: Addressed both; short-circuit implemented with explicit early-return and added metric labels to canary_metrics.yaml (model, route, env).
Priya Patel: Can we add an e2e perf test that simulates transient latency spikes to validate hysteresis prevents immediate rollback?
Aditi Rao: Added perf-canary integration test dynamic_threshold_flow.test that exercises transient spike and verifies hysteresis behavior.
Ethan Zhou: NIT: move the default sensitivity from 'medium' to 'conservative' in schema; production rollout should be conservative by default.
Aditi Rao: Changed default to 'conservative' and documented impact in migration.md.

Aditi Rao: Noted; added CI note and increased retry on that integration test to reduce flakiness.

release_notes: Added dynamic threshold detector for perf canaries with hysteresis and rollout gating. Exposes new canary policy fields (sensitivity, min_samples, hysteresis_window) and adds telemetry metrics. Default sensitivity set to conservative. Backwards compatible: existing policies continue to work but will not opt-in to new detector unless enabled. See docs/perf-canary/migration.md for details.
notes: Feature gated behind ff:perf/dynamic-threshold. Staging run for 48h showed stable behavior; one flaky integration test required extra retry (noted).
